STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of raw almonds on a white square plate, photographed top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate's diagonal is about 390 px wide, and the side is about 280 px. A square side plate is ~20 cm across the flat, so about 0.07 cm per px. Plate area is roughly 20 x 20 = 400 cm^2 (corners are rounded, so ~370 cm^2). A single almond is about 55 px long, which is 3.0-3.5 cm. That fits a real almond (~2.3 cm), so the plate is probably a bit smaller, ~17 cm across. That gives an area of ~280 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Almonds only.

STEP 4 - Area: The almond pile spans about 250 x 240 px, which is roughly 40% of the plate. Counting suggests ~70 almonds.

STEP 5 - Volume: 40% of 280 cm^2 is ~112 cm^2. At a height of ~1.8 cm (almonds piled 1-2 deep) the envelope is ~200 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds have a bulk density of ~0.6 g/ml, so about 120 g. Cross-check by count: ~70 almonds x 1.2 g is ~85 g, and a few extra on the edge bring it to ~90 g. I'll take about 95 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are ~579 kcal/100 g, so 95 g gives ~550 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A heap of ~70 almonds is about 3 handfuls, which is plausible at ~95 g.
